simple.meaning: לָקַק (lâqaq) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to lick or lap.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 7 times across Judges, 1 Kings, beginning at Judges 7:5. Its contexts include blood, death.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לָקַק (H3952).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: לָקַק (lâqaq) / H3952 is traced through Judges 7:5, Judges 7:6, Judges 7:7, 1 Kings 21:19 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: So he brought down the people to the water; and Yahweh said to Gideon, “Everyone who laps of the water with his tongue, like a dog laps, you shall set him by himself; likewise everyone who bows down on his knees to drink.”

timeline.evidenceText: So he brought down the people to the water; and Yahweh said to Gideon, “Everyone who laps of the water with his tongue, like a dog laps, you shall set him by himself; likewise everyone who bows down on his knees to drink.”

So he brought down the people to the water; and Yahweh said to Gideon, “Everyone who laps of the water with his tongue, like a dog laps, you shall set him by himself; likewise everyone who bows down on his knees to drink.”
The number of those who lapped, putting their hand to their mouth, was three hundred men; but all the rest of the people bowed down on their knees to drink water.
Yahweh said to Gideon, “I will save you by the three hundred men who lapped, and deliver the Midianites into your hand. Let all the other people go, each to his own place.”

You shall speak to him, saying, ‘Yahweh says, “Have you killed and also taken possession?” ’ You shall speak to him, saying, ‘Yahweh says, “In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth, dogs will lick your blood, even yours.” ’ ”

definitions.full: H3952. laqaq [ לָקַק ] verb lap, lick (Late Hebrew id. , Pi`el; Arabic lick, lap of dog (Wahrm)); — Qal Perfect 3masculine singular לָֽקְקוּ 1Kin 21:19 ; Imperfect 3masculine singular יָלֹק Judg 7:5 (twice in verse); 3masculine plural יָלֹ֫קּוּ 1Kin 21:19 , וַיָּלֹ֫קּוּ 22:38 ; — lap , הַמַּיִם מִןֿ בִּלְשׁוֺנוֺ יָלֹק Judg 7:5 , like of dog 7:5 (absolute); of dogs lapping up blood (accusative), 1Kin 21:19 (twice in verse); 22:38 . Pi`el Participle plural with article הַמְֿלַקְקִים Judg 7:6 ( אֶלמִּֿיהֶם בְּיָדָם is erroneous gloss, see GFM), 7:7 ; in both = lap, lap up (= Oal Judg 7:5 ). לקשׁ (√ of following; Late Hebrew לקשׁ be late (Hiph`il and derivatives ); Aramaic make or do late , לְקִישָׁא , late ; vulgar Arabic be late (Hauran), Wetzst in De Job 24:6 , so II. Wahrm; late , Dozy Suppl. ii. 543 ).
